extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing a manuscript for submission to BMC Public Health
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts (research articles, reviews, protocols, databases, software, etc.) to the journal BMC Public Health, covering scope, formatting, data and file requirements, licensing, fees, peer review and related editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure submission is to the most suitable journal; BMC Public Health considers articles on epidemiology and all aspects of public health with special focus on social determinants, environmental/behavioral/occupational correlates, and impact of policies/practices/interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should confirm their manuscript fits the journal’s broad topic list (biostatistics, chronic disease epidemiology, digital health, environmental health, global health, health policy, etc.) before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific validity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are based on scientific validity rather than perceived interest or impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts must have a scientifically sound research question, use suitable methods and analysis, and adhere to community-agreed standards within the research field. Diverse perspectives are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charge (APC) and publication fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An APC applies to each accepted article; current APC listed (with currency conversions). Fee is subject to VAT/local taxes and determined from the date of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the applicable APC for their country (country-tiered pricing pilot). See open access support portal and Journal pricing FAQs for eligibility and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access benefits and funder compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing open access increases reach, citations, downloads and Altmetric attention and often enables compliance with funder open access policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider OA for wider readership and to meet funder/institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access funding, discounts and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature offers institutional agreements, funder/institutional support, and discretionary APC waivers/discounts; automatic waivers for corresponding authors based in the lowest income countries are available per policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check open access agreements and waivers policy. Applications for discretionary waivers/discounts must be made at the point of manuscript submission; requests during review or after acceptance cannot be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and copyright (Creative Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are published under CC BY-NC-ND or CC BY licences; authors retain copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC BY-NC-ND: share non-commercially with attribution; permission required for commercial reuse or derivatives. CC BY: share and adapt (including commercially) with attribution. Authors can request licence variations to meet funder/institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare main manuscript text — general formatting (quick points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use double-line spacing, include line and page numbering, use SI units, embed special characters, and do not use page breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure special characters are embedded to avoid loss during PDF conversion. Follow formatting rules for specific article types (research article, review, protocol, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable main manuscript file formats and editable files requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable formats: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich Text Format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX. Editable files are required for production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-editable files (e.g., PDFs) are submitted, authors will be required to re-submit editable versions when revisions are requested or after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX/LaTeX preparation and source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template; pdfLaTeX and TexLive 2021 will be used to compile PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All relevant editable source files must be uploaded during submission; failing to do so will delay production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials availability expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: BioMed Central journals strongly encourage or require authors to provide all datasets on which conclusions rely, via public repositories or as additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide datasets in machine-readable formats (e.g., spreadsheets, not PDFs). Where community expectations exist for repository archiving, deposition is mandatory. Include an 'Availability of data and materials' section with the required wording and persistent identifiers (DOI/accession).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of 'Availability of data and materials' section
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific required phrasing for data availability statements depending on where data are stored or included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data are in a repository: "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink to dataset(s) in https:// format]." If included as additional files: use the alternative required sentence. Publicly available datasets must be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or DOI (Force11 principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation and Force11 Data Citation Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available datasets must be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or unique identifier such as a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For databases, state the web/ftp address and any restrictions to use by non-academics. Follow Force11 principles for data citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference eligibility and good citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Only articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published, are in press, or are available through public e-print/preprint servers may be cited in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be in the reference list but may be mentioned in text as "unpublished observations" or "personal communications" (obtain permission). Only footnotes are permitted. Follow journal-specific reference style (Index Medicus/MEDLINE conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to format web links and URLs in references
rubrics_metrics.description: All web links and URLs should be given a reference number and included in the reference list rather than within the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the title, full URL and the date accessed in the reference list. If an author/group can be associated with the web link, include them. Example format provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: numbering, multi-panel and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered in the order they are first mentioned in the text. Multi-panel figures should be submitted as a single composite file containing all parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload figures in the order they are cited and ensure orientation is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: titles, legends and keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide figure titles (max 15 words) and legends (max 300 words) in the main manuscript (not in the graphic file). Figure keys should be incorporated into the graphic, not the legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all essential explanatory text is in the manuscript; keep title and legend within word limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: cropping, legibility and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should be closely cropped to minimise white space; design figures so all information (including text) is legible at final sizes. Obtain permission for reproducing previously published figures and indicate permission/source in the legend and reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close cropping improves accuracy in layout. Permission must be obtained for figures from non-open access sources; indicate in legend and reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: acceptable file types and file size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure file formats include EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX. Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose suitable format for figure type (e.g., TIFF/JPEG for images, EPS/PDF for diagrams). If suitable, PDF vector figures are preferred for compactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: size and resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Web figures: 600 px (standard) or 1200 px (high resolution). Final PDF widths: 85 mm (half page), 170 mm (full page); maximum height 225 mm. Image resolution ~300 dpi at final size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design figures so text is legible at these dimensions. All lines should be wider than 0.25 pt when scaled to standard widths. All fonts must be embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: file compression and image quality guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector figures should if possible be submitted as PDF. TIFF files should use LZW (lossless) compression. JPEG files should be saved at maximum quality. Minimise conversions between formats to avoid degradation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these recommendations to reduce file size without reducing quality and to avoid image degradation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: numbering, placement and large tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered and cited in sequence using Arabic numerals. Tables shorter than one A4/Letter page can be placed within the manuscript; larger tables should be placed at the end or uploaded as additional files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate where large tables should appear in the text if placed at the end. Very large/wide tables can be uploaded as additional files (Excel or CSV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: titles, legends and formatting restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Table titles (max 15 words) should be above the table; legends (max 300 words) should be below. Tables must be formatted as 'Table object' (not embedded as figures/spreadsheets). Color and shading may not be used. Do not use commas to indicate numerical values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use superscripts, numbering, lettering, symbols or bold text to highlight parts, and explain meanings in the legend. Contact customer service for table-related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: what to include and publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may provide datasets, tables, movies or other information as additional files; all additional files are published with the accepted article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include files such as patient consent forms, certificates of language editing, or revised manuscripts with tracked changes. Provide data that would be 'data not shown' as additional files. Do not link to data on personal/departmental websites—deposit or include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: naming, citation and metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional files should be named 'Additional file 1' etc. Each additional file should be cited in sequence in the main text and a separate section of the manuscript should list file name, format, title and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum file size per additional file is 20 MB; files will be virus-scanned. Use standard file extensions and include a URL of an appropriate viewer if format is unusual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: acceptable formats for tabular data
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabular data provided as additional files can be uploaded as Excel spreadsheets (.xls) or comma-separated values (.csv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard extensions and ensure the file is machine-readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing supporting information — required submission elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must have available: full names and emails for all co-authors; a cover letter addressing specified items; declaration of competing interests; confirmation all authors approved submission; confirmation content not published/submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter should explain why the manuscript should be published in BMC Public Health and explain any issues relating to journal policies. If submitting to a special issue, state the special issue name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter: recommended content for reviewer suggestions and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest potential peer reviewers (provide institutional emails or identifiers such as ORCID/Scopus ID) and may list people they prefer not to review the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falsifying reviewer information (false names/emails) will result in rejection and possible misconduct investigation. Provide verifiable contact details where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and editing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting work in well-written English helps editors and reviewers evaluate fairly. Help is available (tutorials, colleague review, professional language editing services and a free language quality checker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using language services is optional and does not guarantee editorial selection or acceptance. Springer Nature offers author services (discount on first use) and an AI-based language quality checker via partner AJE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria used by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically two or more experts evaluate manuscripts on three main criteria: scientific robustness, originality, and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific robustness: methodology sound and data support conclusions. Originality: does not duplicate published work. Clarity: manuscript is coherent and clear enough for publication. Editors make decisions based on reviewers' reports and may consult editorial board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review and reviewer anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal operates a transparent peer review system where reviewer reports are published alongside the article under CC BY 4.0, but reviewers are not named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published reports can serve educational purposes and advance research into peer review. Reviewers and editors are required to declare competing interests; those with competing interests may be excluded from review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript submission eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submitting person is an author. Follow the submission procedures and supporting information checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer option and Transfer Desk process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is not accepted, authors may be offered transfer to another journal within the Springer Nature portfolio; transfers can save time and avoid reformatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer Desk Editorial Submission Advisors match preferences and editor recommendations with journal-matching technology. Transfer requires author input and agreement. Authors can decline or withdraw a transfer at any point by contacting the Transfer Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and process for APC waiver/discount requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for discretionary APC waivers and discounts must be made at the point of manuscript submission; requests made during the review process or after acceptance cannot be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors needing financial support should apply early and check the waivers/discounts policy for eligibility and required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and database submission metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For software submissions, include project name, project home page, archived version DOI/identifier, operating systems, programming language, other requirements, license, and any restrictions to use by non-academics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient metadata to allow readers to access and run the software; include license information (e.g., GNU GPL) and indicate any access restrictions.
